title: SITE-STATE-1's `soon` seed silences the availability sweep in every local and test database, and the contract does not list the tests that depend on it
why_needed: The contract adds `(select mode from public.site_state) = 'open'` to finance.availability_sweep() and seeds the row `soon` (SITE-STATE-CONTRACT.md lines 34 and 64). Today tests/integration/notify.test.ts (sweep helper line 74, describe at 630), tests/integration/notify-http.test.ts (line 71) and tests/e2e/orders.spec.ts (lines 1017, 1036) call the sweep and expect availability mail; after the migration they get 0 and fail, and the local dev site never sends an availability notice. None of these files, nor a local seed of `open`, is in the contract's exact paths, so the worker either breaks pnpm test:db or edits files outside its allowlist.
touches: PLANS/SITE-STATE-CONTRACT.md (Exact paths, Tests), supabase/seed.sql or a test helper that sets site_state to open, tests/integration/notify.test.ts, tests/integration/notify-http.test.ts, tests/e2e/orders.spec.ts

title: A restore into a new Supabase project disconnects the site-state gate (and the static build) from the database
why_needed: docs/operations.md 'A real restore into a new hosted project' (lines 1332-1410) creates a project with a new <project-ref>. The planned gate reads `GET <SUPABASE_URL>/rest/v1/site_state` with a publishable key held as Worker variables (SITE-STATE-CONTRACT.md line 43); after a restore it keeps reading the dead project, every read fails, and the domain silently follows MODE while the owner's «حالة الموقع» switch (now on the new project) changes nothing. The contract names MODE=maintenance as the switch 'for a restore', but neither the contract nor the restore steps say: deploy MODE=maintenance before step 2, then repoint the gate's SUPABASE_URL and key (and rebuild the Pages site with the new NEXT_PUBLIC Supabase address), then MODE back to open.
touches: docs/operations.md (restore steps), PLANS/SITE-STATE-CONTRACT.md, the P11 runbook lines (docs/rollback.md, docs/deployment.md)

title: The gate must cover every hostname that reaches the Pages project, and the contract does not say which it covers: a Worker route covers only the hostnames it names (www and pages.dev stay open), a Pages Function covers all of them (and blocks pre-launch testing of the shop)
why_needed: SITE-STATE-CONTRACT.md line 56 assumes pages.dev is outside the gate. A Pages Function (_middleware) is part of the deployment, so it also answers on <project>.pages.dev and preview deployments: while the stored state is `soon` (seeded, and until «افتح الموقع») /store, /cart and /checkout are hidden on every hostname, and the hosted P08/E02 proof and P10's hosted checks of the shop need either `open` (which also opens the real domain, since both read the same row) or a bypass the contract does not define. With a Worker route the opposite holds and pages.dev exposes the whole unlaunched site. P11's choice should record which, and how testers reach the shop before launch (for example Access-protected pages.dev, or a bypass only for Access-authenticated requests). A Worker route is per hostname: the contract and README move both anas.studio and www to the Pages project, but name only "the gate in front of the Pages project"; a route on anas.studio/* alone leaves https://www.anas.studio serving the unlaunched site during soon and the launched one during maintenance. Until the domain is on Pages, the stored row must also stay soon on every database the gate reads: worker.js is today the Custom Domain origin itself, so an open answer would have no site to pass to (a fetch to its own hostname calls the Custom Domain Worker again; https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/routing/custom-domains/).

title: The gate sets a first-party cookie on anas.studio that the privacy data map does not list
why_needed: worker.js line 35 sets soon=<letter> (Path=/, 30 days, HttpOnly) on every soon and maintenance page, and the contract keeps this Worker as the gate in front of the launched site, so the cookie is set on the product domain whenever the state is soon or maintenance and is then sent with every request to the site for 30 days. docs/privacy-data-map.md (the A buyer's browser row, line 25) lists only localStorage and sessionStorage; the privacy text E08 approves is written from that map.
